To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction of 1-methtyl-2-thiourea (N-methylthiourea, NMTU) with chloro- and bromoacetic acid and their esters leads to the formation of 8-alkyl-3-oxothiazolo[3.2-a]-pyrimidinones.

8-alkyl-3-oxothiazolo[3.2-a]-pyrimidinium chlorides are obtained from N-methylpropyldithiourea and α-halocarbocyclic acids, and that these salts are readily transformed into the 3-alkyl-1,3-thiadiazolidine-4-diones.

8-methylthiazolo[1,3a]pyrimidinium chloride and bromide can be synthesized by the reaction of N-methylpropyldihiourea with chloro- and bromoacetic acid and their esters, and that the former compound undergoes a hydrolysis reaction in ethanol, which is stopped in a solution of ethanol and water, but the hydrolysis continues when the solution is replaced with pure water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of 3-[(alkylamino)alkyl]-1,2-thiazolidine derivatives, which are of interest as potential antitumor agents.
the synthesis and properties of new 3-[(aminoalkyl)-1,3-thiolane-2,4-]diones.
the synthesis and study of the reactions of the new 3-[(alkylamino)alkyl]-1, 3-thiazolidin-2,4diones, 2-amino-4-(alkylamino)-3,4-dihydrothiazole-5-carboxylates and 2-aminothiazole-4-carboxamides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reaction of N-methylpropyldiourea with chloroacetic acid or its esters is accompanied by the formation of 3-[(2-chloro-3-methylamionopropyl)-amino]-1,3- thiazolidine- 2,4-dionium chloride or bromine and the corresponding hydrobromo- and chloride salts of 8-methylthiazolo[2,3-c]-pyrimidinium.
the alkylation of N-methylpropyldenethiourea with α-haloalkanoic acids and their ester leads to the formation of 3-(alkylamino)alkyl-1,3-thiozolidine-2-4-diones.
the alkylation of N-methylpropylyenethiourea with α-haloacetic acids and esters gives the corresponding 8-alkyl-3-oxotetrahydro-1,3-thiazo-2,4-pyrimidinones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alkylations of 1-methytetrahydropyridine-2(1 H)-thione and 1-methylthiosemicarbazide by α-halogenoacetic acids are not limited to the N-alkylations only.

the alkylations of the 1-methyl- and the 2-methyltetrahydro-2-thiopyrimidines by α-haloketones and α-halocarbono acids and their ester proceed with the attack at the carbon atom of the α-CHX group of the reagent.

the alkylations of the cyclic thioureas with α-halocarbonylic acids and their alkyl esters proceed via the formation of the intermediate N-acyl derivatives which are then hydrolyzed to the corresponding N-alkyl derivatives and finally cyclized to the corresponding 1,3-thiadiazolium salts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the alkylation of cyclic thiourea by the halocarboxy acids and their ester is a general method of the synthesis of the 3-oxothiazolidine derivatives.
the alkylation of cyclic thiourea with α-halocarbonyl compounds can be a useful method of synthesis for the compounds containing the thiocarbonyl moiety.
the alkylated products are obtained as the corresponding salts, which is not a trivial fact, because it is the first time such salts are reported.
